components.cost_effect: Scalar preprocessing; no gradient queries if bounds are already supplied.
components.goal: Choose stationary coefficients for a known quadratic spectral interval.
components.key_estimate: The linked Theorem provides epsilon-geometric norm-error convergence for these parameters.
components.name: Spectral tuning
components.operation: Compute alpha and beta from the supplied m,M using the selected variant formulas.
components.requires: Valid positive spectral bounds and an exact quadratic gradient.
transfer_checks: Recheck the exact quadratic structure and spectral interval.
Do not transfer arbitrary initialization to general nonlinear objectives.

limitations.statement: The original general nonlinear Theorem requires sufficiently close initial points. The quadratic arbitrary-start result does not establish global convergence for general strongly convex smooth objectives.
Noisy gradients, constraints, spectrum estimation and certified adaptive stopping are outside this selected implementation and its performance claim.

performance_links.scope_note: Quadratic norm-error performance only; no unrestricted Oracle Complexity optimality assertion.

variants.cost: Exactly N-1 gradient queries after supplied x0,x1. Each update also uses a fixed number of vector additions/scalings and O(1) stored H-vectors including gradient workspace. In R^d these require O(d) arithmetic and storage, excluding gradient implementation. Parameter evaluation is scalar preprocessing. Estimating m,M, generating x1, objective evaluations and extra stopping tests are separately charged.
variants.implementation_details_ref: Printed p12 Equation (9), p13 Theorem 9(3), p15 quadratic Note; PDF pp13,14,16.
variants.name: Quadratic specialization with optimized parameters
variants.output: Return last iterate x_N. For N=1 return supplied x1.
public_inputs: Real Hilbert space H; exact gradient P(x)=Ax-b.
Known valid bounds 0<m<=M<infinity, with bounded self-adjoint A and mI<=A<=MI.
Supplied x0,x1 in H and integer output horizon N>=1.
variants.query_and_update: For n=1,...,N-1 query g_n=Ax_n-b and set x_{n+1}=x_n-alpha g_n+beta(x_n-x_{n-1}); retain the latest pair.
variants.requirements: Unconstrained quadratic f(x)=<x,Ax>/2-<b,x>+c on all H, b in H; exact deterministic gradient and known spectral bounds.
variants.state_and_initialization: Store arbitrary supplied x0,x1. The first update has n=1. Any procedure used to generate x1 is separately charged.
variants.tuning_and_stopping: alpha=4/(sqrt(M)+sqrt(m))^2 and beta=((sqrt(M)-sqrt(m))/(sqrt(M)+sqrt(m)))^2. Stop at prescribed N. No certified adaptive stopping rule is extracted; accuracy-based tuning must retain the initial-error and epsilon-dependent constants in the linked Theorem.

checked_locators: Visually checked Equation (9), Theorem 9(3) and quadratic Note, PDF pp13–16.

summary: Exact-gradient two-step recurrence with known positive spectral bounds and arbitrary two-point initialization on a quadratic.
title: Polyak heavy-ball method: quadratic specialization
use_when: Apply the stationary heavy-ball recurrence to an unconstrained positive-definite quadratic with known spectral bounds.
